variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: NP_000220.1:p.(Leu212AlafsTer17). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a summary row of a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; data are second-hand from the cited case report.
The nucleotide-change cell runs two variants together ('c.794_801dec.633dupG'); the first is truncated and its exact description is uncertain.
A second LCAT variant is listed; zygosity and phase not reported.
REF 33 does not match the reference list ([33] is an exon-6 missense report; [35] describes two frameshift mutations).
notes_for_panel: Korean male with FLD; the row lists two variants fused into one string, 'c.794_801dec.633dupG', read as c.794_801de(l) and c.633dupG (exons 5 and 6). The REF column says 33, but reference [33] in the list is Maeda et al. 1991 (exon 6 missense), whereas reference [35] is Park et al. 2009, 'Two novel frame shift mutations ... familial LCAT deficiency phenotype', which fits two frameshifts; the source should be checked. Variant written c.633dupG; the batch HGVS is c.633dup (predicted Leu212AlafsTer17).
